issues.description: Function simulate_ghz_state: the template defines simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int) (no shots parameter) while the solution defines simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int). The template's docstring and body refer to a 'shots' argument (assertions and measurement steps), but the signature omits it. This mismatch (template vs solution and problem expectations) will confuse students and break any calls/tests that expect a shots parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to include the shots parameter to match the solution and problem intent: def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int]:. Ensure the function body and docstring use the shots parameter (keep or add the assertion assert shots > 0) and that any example/call sites and tests expect the same signature.
